contract.gap: Connect task-specific face recognition to editable aircraft B-Rep geometry across topology changes, and characterise recognition errors and downstream surface-mesh scale on the recorded developmental set.
contract.task: Recognize rivets and cosmetic features at B-Rep face level and use predictions as candidate inputs to staged CAD processing.
outcomes: fresh staged CAD outcomes and mesh/QEM measurements

questions.text: How accurately does the implemented system identify rivet and cosmetic-feature faces on the developmental aircraft set?
How are recognised faces connected to staged CAD operations after topology changes?
How do the recorded CAD endpoints change surface-mesh size and mesher time under a fixed tessellation policy?

contract.contribution: Task-specific attributed face graphs, recognition-to-editing correspondence, and traceable aircraft case-study evidence. Standard GNN components and categorical output are implementation choices, not independently validated architectural innovations.
nonclaims: No universal generalization claim across all aircraft or CAD sources.
Geometric comparison does not establish physics equivalence.
No CAE acceleration or response-preservation claim before controlled downstream experiments.
No mesh-quality or geometric-fidelity superiority claim over QEM.
Human visual review is not described as fully automatic validation.
Retired BFS and 51-dimensional experiments are not part of the formal model.
No independent test claim for the inspected development set.
No architecture-superiority conclusion from the removed historical comparison.

semantic_locks.canonical: background=0, rivet=1, surface_feature=2 in stored data; manuscript display labels are background, rivet, cosmetic feature. Cosmetic feature denotes annotated non-rivet target faces, including window and decal regions, considered for simplification or reconstruction. Native decal/window provenance remains in JSON.
Dataset partitioning is performed by complete aircraft model, not by randomly splitting faces
The post-classification rivet guard rejects relative face area above 5e-6; the cosmetic-feature class has topology, visibility and density screening, without a single global area cutoff.

The active model has one shared GNN encoder and one categorical head with three logits. Raw inference uses softmax and argmax; the known-geometry completion and suppression chain produces separately stored final labels.

Figures6--11 and CAD/mesh/QEM tables use the current three-class model CAD endpoints. Input CAD colours are original annotations, processed geometry is uniformly shaded. Nine-aircraft results describe a known developmental set.
